as_written_in_papers.quote: p.Asp322fs (c.964delG) annotated to transcript NM_002294.2 in exon 8

cases.statement: Two females of one Polish family (PMID 33224350): the proband with severe HCM and heart transplantation at 18, and her asymptomatic mother; both carry the variant.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: HCM diagnosed at 12 with complex ventricular arrhythmias and ICD; severe heart failure with LVEF 25%; LBBB with fragmented QRS; right ventricular noncompaction; glycogen-containing vacuoles on endomyocardial biopsy; heart transplantation; no intellectual impairment; normal CK

quotes.quote: The 18-year-old woman with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy diagnosed at 12 years, with complex ventricular arrhythmias leading to implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) treatment in primary prevention was referred to the Institute of Cardiology, Warsaw
Left ventricular systolic function was severely decreased (LVEF 25%) with contraction asynchrony (Figure 3 A) and reduced left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (11.7 cm).
Endomyocardial biopsy showed hypertrophic cardiomyocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, severe interstitial fibrosis and the presence of vacuoles containing glycogen (Figures 4 A–D).
Furthermore, noncompaction of the right ventricular myocardium (Figure 3 D) with decreased RV systolic function was noted (TAPSE 10 mm, S′ 5.8 cm/s).
Due to progressive symptoms of heart failure, she was treated with a biventricular assist device for mechanical circulatory support for one month and subsequently received a heart transplant.

people.label: mother of patient
people.key_phenotypes: asymptomatic, with normal ECG, echocardiogram and 24-h Holter

quotes.quote: Subsequent family screening with direct Sanger sequencing confirmed the presence of the truncating variant in the patient’s asymptomatic (based on normal non-invasive cardiac examination – ECG, echocardiogram, Holter 24 h ECG) mother.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Proband: HCM with storage-type vacuoles. TruSight One panel; the authors found no other variant that could influence the disease. The authors note the RV noncompaction may be due to an unidentified gene.

quotes.quote: After receiving written informed consent the patient underwent genetic examination with the TruSight One Sequencing Panel (Illumina), which revealed a frameshift truncating variant in the LAMP2 gene
After careful analysis of the genetic test results of our patient we did not identify any other variants that could influence the clinical course of her disease.
However, we cannot exclude that this finding is related to an unidentified gene.

segregation.statement: The proband's mother carries the variant and is clinically unaffected on non-invasive testing. The father died at 36 of an extracardiac cause and was not tested. No other relatives reported.

quotes.quote: Subsequent family screening with direct Sanger sequencing confirmed the presence of the truncating variant in the patient’s asymptomatic (based on normal non-invasive cardiac examination – ECG, echocardiogram, Holter 24 h ECG) mother.
Her father died at the age of 36 years due to an extracardiac cause, and her mother was asymptomatic with normal noninvasive cardiological examinations.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the proband: inherited from her mother. The mother's parents are not reported as tested.

quotes.quote: A novel frameshift mutation p.Asp322fs (c.964delG) annotated to transcript NM_002294.2 was identified in the proband and her asymptomatic mother.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift (predicted p.(Asp322MetfsTer24)). The authors relate the disease to LAMP2 deficiency and propose skewed X-inactivation (not tested) for the difference between proband and mother.

quotes.quote: Similarly as in our patient, the majority of mutations identified in Danon disease are predicted to cause LAMP2 deficiency [4].
One possible explanation is skewed X-inactivation in the proband, which could lead to increased mutation dosage, leading to a severe clinical picture compared to the mother

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel truncating variant; no ACMG classification is given.

quotes.quote: A novel truncating variant in the LAMP2 gene in a young woman with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and variable clinical course in the family

concerns: Transcript stated as NM_002294.2; the batch uses NM_002294.3. The protein is given only as p.Asp322fs (no new residue or stop position).
The proband's mother is an unaffected carrier; X-inactivation was not measured.
Right ventricular noncompaction in the proband is called unusual for Danon disease by the authors.
Zygosity is never stated for either female.
notes_for_panel: Mother-to-daughter transmission with discordant expression (severe HCM vs no findings); the proband has biopsy evidence of glycogen-containing vacuoles and a panel with no other relevant variant.
